Wedding Mantras

Sacred verses chanted at South Indian weddings, for blessings on the new life together.

Ganesha Vandana

वक्रतुण्ड महाकाय सूर्यकोटि समप्रभ ।
निर्विघ्नं कुरु मे देव सर्वकार्येषु सर्वदा ॥

Vakratunda Mahakaya Suryakoti Samaprabha | Nirvighnam Kuru Me Deva Sarvakaryeshu Sarvada ||

O Lord with the curved trunk and mighty form, radiant as a million suns, remove all obstacles from every undertaking, always.

Mangalya Dharana

माङ्गल्यं तन्तुनानेन मम जीवनहेतुना ।
कण्ठे बध्नामि सुभगे त्वं जीव शरदः शतम् ॥

Mangalyam Tantunanena Mama Jivana Hetuna | Kanthe Badhnami Subhage Tvam Jiva Sharadah Shatam ||

With this sacred thread, on which my life depends, I tie the knot around your neck, O fortunate one. May you live a hundred autumns.

Saptapadi

सखा सप्तपदी भव

Sakha Saptapadi Bhava

Take these seven steps with me and be my friend for life.

Devi Prarthana

सर्वमङ्गलमाङ्गल्ये शिवे सर्वार्थसाधिके ।
शरण्ये त्र्यम्बके गौरि नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते ॥

Sarva Mangala Mangalye Shive Sarvartha Sadhike | Sharanye Tryambake Gauri Narayani Namostu Te ||

O auspicious Gauri, giver of every blessing and fulfilment, refuge of all, we bow to you.

Wedding Rituals

The sacred ceremonies of a Telugu wedding, in the order they are traditionally followed.

గోరింటాకుGorintaku

Henna is applied to the bride’s hands and feet before the wedding.

పెళ్లికూతురు & పెళ్లికొడుకుPellikuthuru & Pellikoduku

Married women apply turmeric, oil and kumkum to the bride and the groom at their homes.

మంగళస్నానంMangala Snanam

The sacred turmeric bath on the wedding morning.

సమావర్తనం / స్నాతకంSamavarthana · Snathakam

The groom sets out for Kashi, and the bride’s father stops him and offers his daughter in marriage.

ఎదురుకోలుEdurukolu

The bride’s family welcomes the groom and his family at the venue.

వ్రతంVratham

The couple perform the sacred vratham together with a kalasam, rice and prayers, seeking blessings before the wedding rituals begin.

గౌరీ పూజGouri Puja

The bride worships Goddess Gouri for a happy married life.

వరమాలVaramala

The couple exchange flower garlands.

గణేశ పూజGanesha Puja

The bride and groom seek Lord Ganesha’s blessings for a happy marriage and the removal of obstacles.

వధువు ప్రవేశం / తెరసాలBride’s Entry & Terasala

The bride is escorted to the mandapam by her maternal uncle and aunt under a flower canopy. A curtain (terasala) is held between the couple until the muhurtham.

కన్యాదానంKanyadanam

The bride’s parents give their daughter’s hand to the groom.

పాణిగ్రహణంPanigrahanam

The groom holds the bride’s hand and promises her father, three times, to remain her companion in joy and sorrow forever.

జీలకర్ర బెల్లంJilakarra Bellam

At the auspicious moment, the couple place a paste of cumin and jaggery on each other’s heads.

మధుపర్కం / సుమంగళిMadhuparkam & Sumangali

The bride wears traditional ceremonial attire, surrounded by married women carrying sacred rice, flowers and lamps.

మాంగల్యధారణMangalya Dharana

The groom ties the sacred mangalsutra around the bride’s neck.

బ్రహ్మముడిBrahmamudi

The sacred knots are tied in the mangalsutra thread, with the groom’s sister helping to secure them, binding the couple together.

నల్లపూసలుNalla Pusalu

The groom adorns the bride with the traditional black-bead necklace, symbolizing her married status.

తలంబ్రాలుTalambralu

The couple shower each other with rice mixed with turmeric, a joyful and playful ritual.

సప్తపదిSaptapadi

The couple take seven steps together and make their vows.

స్థాలీపాకంSthalipakam

The groom adorns the bride’s feet with silver toe rings (mettelu), a sign of a married woman.

ప్రధానంPradhanam

The bride and groom playfully search for a ring in a decorated vessel of water while family members cheer them on.

అరుంధతీ దర్శనంArundhati Darshanam

The couple look at the Arundhati star, the symbol of a faithful and steady marriage.

ఆశీర్వాదంAshirvadam

The newly married couple bow before their elders to receive blessings for a happy and prosperous married life.

అప్పగింతలుAppagintalu

The emotional farewell where the bride receives her parents’ blessings before leaving with the groom.

గృహప్రవేశంGruhapravesam

The newly married bride enters her new home, gently pushing a rice-filled vessel with her right foot as the groom and family welcome her.

సత్యనారాయణ వ్రతంSatyanarayana Vratam

The newly married couple perform the Satyanarayana Puja with a priest, traditional offerings and the blessings of Lord Satyanarayana.

మంగళసూత్రాల కలయికUniting the Mangalasutram

The two sacred mangalsutras are joined together on one thread, traditionally around the 16th day after marriage in some Telugu families.

The order may vary slightly by family tradition.
